description: Dedicated entries for Dunhallow Roost leaders, residents, and Hollow's End patrons.

entries.title: Mayor Elvira Caelwind
entries.summary: Dunhallow's pragmatic former merchant is secretly seeking illicit food supplies after a devastating tithe.
body: Elvira took control of [[dunhallow-roost|Dunhallow Roost]] after the previous mayor vanished under suspicious circumstances. Her trading experience helps her manage a settlement stripped of surplus food and wealth.
With families nearing starvation, she is quietly negotiating with smugglers. The arrangement may save the town while exposing her leadership to criminal leverage and draconic retaliation.

entries.title: Harbormaster Ryn Goldfenn
entries.summary: A sociable halfling harbormaster manages Dunhallow's small docks and collects the settlement's passing gossip.
body: Ryn oversees the floating docks used by vessels visiting [[dunhallow-roost|Dunhallow Roost]]. His work places him at the center of arrivals, departures, cargo movements, and local rumor.
He enjoys knowing everyone's business, making him a useful source of information and a likely first witness to smugglers, tithe agents, pirates, or unfamiliar ships.

entries.title: Brother Varic
entries.summary: A Dwarven priest and retired adventurer increasingly argues that Dunhallow must resist draconic tithes.
body: Brother Varic serves the Skyward and offers spiritual guidance to [[dunhallow-roost|Dunhallow Roost]]. His long life and adventuring experience give his warnings unusual weight among frightened residents.
The latest tithe has made him openly critical of submission. His calls for resistance may strengthen the town's resolve or provoke action it lacks the weapons and supplies to survive.

entries.title: Jakrin the Weasel
entries.summary: A known smuggler offers Dunhallow illegal routes to food while the settlement approaches starvation.
body: Jakrin arrived in [[dunhallow-roost|Dunhallow Roost]] after the tithe fleet stripped away much of the community's food. He promises alternative supply methods whose illegality is barely concealed.

His offer makes him useful to [[elvira-caelwind|Mayor Elvira Caelwind]] and dangerous to everyone involved. Hidden prices, criminal partners, and draconic enforcement may matter as much as the food he can deliver.

entries.title: Old Marrok
entries.summary: A retired Dwarven mercenary trades embellished war stories for drinks at Hollow's End.
body: Old Marrok spends his days at [[hollows-end-tavern|Hollow's End Tavern]], where free rounds can buy one of his many war stories. The stories are only half true, though listeners may disagree about which half.
His mercenary past gives him fragments of military and faction knowledge, while his exaggeration makes every useful detail require corroboration.

entries.title: Serka the Wanderer
entries.summary: A quiet Dragonborn bounty hunter watches Hollow's End from the corner while waiting between contracts.
body: Serka rarely speaks unless approached and habitually observes the room at [[hollows-end-tavern|Hollow's End Tavern]]. Her profession makes the neutral-ground ban on apprehending targets particularly relevant.
Whether she is truly between jobs or using the tavern to study a future quarry is left uncertain.

entries.title: The Tattered Captain
entries.summary: A concealed monthly visitor to Hollow's End pays in gems and speaks through heavy magical distortion.
body: The Tattered Captain arrives at [[hollows-end-tavern|Hollow's End Tavern]] once each month. The hooded visitor never removes their gloves and offers gems rather than ordinary coin.
A magically distorted voice prevents easy identification. The regular schedule suggests deliberate business, surveillance, or exchange beneath the appearance of an anonymous traveler.
